Other words

  • dēsipiēns, dēsipientis — foolish, silly

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 153, 157

  • dēsipiō, dēsipere — to be silly, act foolishly

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 157

  • ineptiō, ineptīre — to act or talk foolishly

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 5.8.11 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 153

    (Lewis & Short: comic and poetic)

  • ineptia, ineptiae f. — silliness, nonsense

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 4.7.31 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 157

    Lewis & Short: in the singular early and late Latin; classical prose has the plural ineptiae.

  • dēsipientia, dēsipientiae f. — foolishness

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Lucr. 3.499 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 153

  • dēlīrātiō, dēlīrātiōnis f. — silliness, folly, dotage

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 157

See also don’t be silly!.
